settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Parse errors are caught (catch Throwable, lines 153-157) and evaluation errors catch SpelEvaluationException/Throwable (lines 220-227), logging rather than failing; this only limits error handling, not expression capability.
selectorHeaderInUse defaults to false and filterSubscriptions returns immediately when no selector was ever parsed (lines 191-193), so evaluation only happens after a selector was supplied.

The evaluation blocks are wrapped in try/catch, so an expression that throws would be swallowed rather than surfacing - which reduces visible crash-based signals but does not prevent side effects of invoked methods.
candidates.description:
DefaultSubscriptionRegistry holds an ExpressionParser backed by SpelExpressionParser (line 76). In addSubscriptionInternal, the value of the client-controlled native header named by selectorHeaderName (default "selector", line 72) is taken from the message headers via SimpMessageHeaderAccessor.getFirstNativeHeader (line 144) and passed without validation to expressionParser.parseExpression(selector) (line 147). The parsed expression is stored on the subscription (line 159) and later evaluated in filterSubscriptions with expression.getValue(context, boolean.class) (line 216) using a StandardEvaluationContext whose root object is the message and where a SimpMessageHeaderPropertyAccessor is registered (lines 212-213). The STOMP header reaches this code unmodified: StompSubProtocolHandler.handleMessageFromClient decodes client WebSocket frames (decoder.decode, line 252) and forwards the resulting Message, including client native headers, through outputChannel.send(message) (line 299); SUBSCRIBE frames are recognized as StompCommand.SUBSCRIBE (line 312) and are not stripped of the selector native header in the read range. Because SpEL with StandardEvaluationContext permits method invocation and type references by default, a STOMP client that can open a subscription could supply a selector such as a type-reference/method-invocation expression, yielding expression injection beyond simple header comparison; the class javadoc itself states the selector header "can use Spring EL expressions against message headers" (lines 53-55, 113-116).

Evidence of the flow: header value -> parseExpression (no allowlist/regex/sanitization between lines 144-147), expression retained (159), evaluation context built from the message (212-213), evaluated (216). The bounds/try-catch at lines 153-157 and 220-227 only log parse/evaluation failures (logged at debug/trace); they are not input restrictions.
missing_evidence: SimpleBrokerMessageHandler was not read, so the exact call path from the SUBSCRIBE message to DefaultSubscriptionRegistry.addSubscriptionInternal is inferred, not verified in source.
StompDecoder / StompHeaderAccessor were not read, so the precise mapping of raw STOMP frame headers to the "selector" native header is not verified (the file listing shows these exist).

No runtime/configuration inspection was possible: whether type references/method invocation are reachable in the effective evaluation context, and whether any application interceptor blocks the selector header, is unverified.
Only lines 1-120 and 120-319 of DefaultSubscriptionRegistry and 200-330 of StompSubProtocolHandler were read; the remaining lines of both files were not inspected.
preconditions: A running messaging application exposes the STOMP-over-WebSocket endpoint with a SimpleBroker / DefaultSubscriptionRegistry (broker registry), and the client is able to send STOMP SUBSCRIBE frames.

No deployment-level mechanism (e.g., an inbound interceptor, channel security or selectorHeaderName disablement) rejects or sanitizes the selector native header before it reaches DefaultSubscriptionRegistry.addSubscriptionInternal.
SpEL type references and method invocation are available in the StandardEvaluationContext used at evaluation time (default SpelExpressionParser behavior; not verified at runtime).
candidates.title: Client-supplied STOMP 'selector' header evaluated as Spring EL expression in DefaultSubscriptionRegistry
